name: Vulvar Intraepithelial Neoplasia
aliases: Squamous Intraepithelial Lesion of the Vulva

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for VIN

criteria.description: Presence of dysplastic squamous epithelial cells confined to the vulvar epithelium without stromal invasion
Identification of vulvar lesions such as white, red, or pigmented plaques or papules on physical examination
Detection of high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) DNA in lesion tissue, especially HPV 16

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of epithelial dysplasia confined to the vulvar epithelium with compatible clinical lesion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Biopsy is essential to differentiate VIN from invasive vulvar carcinoma and benign vulvar dermatoses.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Persistent vulvar pruritus localized to lesion
pathognomonic.notes: Often refractory to standard antipruritic treatments
searchTerms: ongoing vulvar itch localized to lesion

pathognomonic.symptomName: Visible vulvar leukoplakic or erythematous plaques
searchTerms: white or red patches on vulva

pathognomonic.symptomName: Vulvar burning sensation localized to affected area

searchTerms: pain during intercourse from vulvar lesions
discomfort with sex due to vulvar growth
fluid or pus from vulvar lesion
dark spots or bumps on vulva

occasional.symptomName: Localized vulvar edema with mild pain
searchTerms: localized vulvar swelling with mild pain
spotting from vulva unrelated to menstruation

rare.symptomName: Secondary bacterial infection of vulvar lesion
searchTerms: pus or infection in vulvar wound

rare.notes: May suggest progression to invasive carcinoma

laboratory: Histopathological evidence of squamous epithelial dysplasia without stromal invasion
HPV DNA testing positive for high-risk subtypes (e.g., HPV 16)
imaging: Pelvic MRI or ultrasound may be used to exclude invasive disease if clinically suspected
genetic: No specific germline mutations identified; HPV-related oncogenic pathways implicated
other: Colposcopic examination of vulvar lesions for detailed assessment

distinguishingFeatures: Chronic inflammatory dermatosis with white atrophic plaques
Absence of epithelial dysplasia on biopsy
Invasion of stromal tissue on histopathology
Presence of palpable mass or ulceration

references: Jones RW, Rowan DM. Vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia: diagnosis and management. Obstet Gynecol. 2017;130(3):e123-e130.
